for_davis: For your Sprint 2 project, Le Chonk is a free open-weight frontier coding model you can self-host and run small evals on instead of burning API credits. The Cursor incidents are a practical security checklist for your approval-gated follow-up system: verify extensions, keep browsers sandboxed, never let an agent act on hidden instructions. And the boomerang story is the market thesis for your career move — companies are re-hiring for the humans who can run the AI.
headline: Le Chonk goes open-weight; Gemini 4 Carbon tops the index; coding tools hit by security pile-up

stories.summary: Mistral published the downloadable weights for Mistral Large 4 on Oct 29, weeks after its Oct 6 preview. The 1.05-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model (52B active) has a 1M-token context window and is pitched at coding, agents and cybersecurity; Mistral claims top open-weight scores on agentic coding benchmarks. The release came with a ~50% API price cut ($0.70/$2.10 per million tokens) and was the day's top Hacker News story.
stories.title: Mistral releases open weights of Large 4, the 1T-parameter 'Le Chonk'
stories.why_it_matters: A frontier-class open model you can actually download changes what a solo builder can run locally — and the sovereignty pitch matters for government-adjacent work.

stories.summary: Google DeepMind took the wraps off Gemini 4 Carbon on Oct 29, calling it its strongest model yet for cybersecurity and long-horizon engineering. It leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 at 59, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (58) and GPT-6 Astra (57), topping vulnerability finding (SEC-bench Pro 88.2%), exploitation (ExploitGym 54.8%) and patching (CWE-bench 71.0%). Access is deliberately narrow at first: a subset of trusted cyber defenders via Google's Fairwind program, priced at $2/$10 per million tokens.
stories.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier model built for cyber defence
stories.why_it_matters: The tiered defender-first rollout is a new release pattern worth watching — frontier capability is being aimed at cyber defence first.

stories.summary: Forever Security disclosed research on Oct 29 finding the embedded browsers in Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Anthropic's Claude Desktop, Microsoft VS Code and OpenAI's Codex are over-privileged, enabling code execution, file theft or address-bar spoofing. Cursor silently patched its flaw on Oct 1 after a Sep 10 disclosure; GitHub fixed Copilot independently on Oct 13; the VS Code and Codex flaws remain unpatched.
stories.title: 'Embrace': embedded-browser flaws found in five AI coding tools
stories.why_it_matters: You build daily in Cursor and Claude Code — know which surfaces are unpatched, and treat anything a tool's browser shows you as untrusted input.

stories.summary: Reuters reported Oct 30 that a maliciously modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension was live on Cursor's extension marketplace for roughly 11 hours on Thursday, collecting host and user details and attempting to set up remote access. Cursor shut down and rebuilt the marketplace as a precaution; the extension was not developed by Anthropic.
stories.title: Cursor pulls tampered Claude Code extension after up to 5,000 users affected
stories.why_it_matters: Extension marketplaces are now an attack surface on your dev machine — verify what you install, especially lookalikes of tools you trust.

stories.summary: A Washington Post report (Oct 30) cites Careerminds data: a third of companies that laid off workers citing AI have rehired 25-50% of the roles, and another 35.6% rehired more than half — mostly within six months, citing more oversight needed than expected. Microsoft offered voluntary exits to ~60,000 employees; Gartner projects 30% of AI-displaced workers rehired by 2029. Stanford payroll data shows the entry-level squeeze persists: 22-25-year-olds in AI-exposed occupations are ~19% behind peers, driven by fewer hires.
stories.title: The 'AI boomerang': a third of AI-led layoffs are being reversed
stories.why_it_matters: The cuts overshot — employers want the humans who can run the AI. That's the lane you're training for: applied AI implementation, not credentials alone.

tldr: Two frontier moves in 24 hours: Mistral released the open weights of its 1T-parameter Large 4, and Google unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon, a cyber-defence-focused frontier model now leading the Artificial Analysis index. Meanwhile researchers disclosed embedded-browser flaws in five AI coding tools, and Cursor pulled a tampered Claude Code extension after up to 5,000 users were affected. The AI-labor story flipped: a third of companies that cut jobs citing AI have quietly started rehiring them.
